original_question: Suppose that A ⊂ [0, 1] is open and has measure greater than 13 . Is there a solution to xy = z?
target_in_source: Ben Green, 100 Open Problems, section 1 (“Sum-free sets, product-free sets”), Problem 3, page 4. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft is already very close to the source statement: it correctly identifies the ambient interval [0,1], the openness hypothesis, the threshold 1/3, and the multiplicative relation xy = z as the forbidden configuration under discussion. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: It should explicitly say that the sought solution is a triple x, y, z all belonging to A. The source’s question is whether A contains such a multiplicative triple. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))

It should specify that “measure” means Lebesgue measure μ on [0,1], as indicated by the nearby comments using μ(Aθ). ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))

The surrounding context is that this is a product-free-set problem: one asks whether an open subset of [0,1] of measure greater than 1/3 can still avoid all triples x, y, z in A with xy = z. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))

A key source-critical detail is that the constant 1/3 is intended to be sharp: the comments give explicit open product-free examples Aθ = {x : θ log x ∈ (1/3, 2/3) (mod 1)} with μ(Aθ) = t/(t^2 + t + 1), where t = e^(1/(3θ)), and μ(Aθ) tends to 1/3 as θ → ∞. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))

The source does not broaden the problem to arbitrary measurable sets, so the openness hypothesis should be retained exactly as stated. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: If A is an open subset of [0,1] with Lebesgue measure μ(A) > 1/3, must there exist x, y, z ∈ A such that xy = z?
justification: Problem 3 in Green’s document states the question essentially verbatim. The adjacent comments provide the main hidden context needed for a stand-alone formulation: this is a question about product-free subsets of [0,1], and Green records an explicit family Aθ showing that the threshold 1/3 cannot be lowered. The refinement therefore keeps the original hypotheses exactly, while making explicit that the solution sought is a triple x, y, z lying in A and that μ denotes Lebesgue measure. ([people.maths.ox.ac.uk](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf))
